code:
Authenticated user: one person, one session,
                    individually auditable

Guest user: EVERY anonymous visitor,
            same profile, same access,
            worldwide, simultaneously
caption: A guest-user mistake can expose data to the entire internet, not just employees.

eyebrow: Secure guest user record access — mandatory since Summer '20

steps.label: Can't be disabled
steps.sub: a platform floor, not an admin preference

steps.label: Explicit grants only
steps.sub: sharing rule or sharing set, not OWD alone

steps.label: Remove unneeded object access
steps.sub: review every permission on the profile

steps.label: Disable API Enabled
steps.sub: unless the site specifically needs it

steps.label: Create, not Read, for forms
steps.sub: grant only what the function needs

steps.label: Sharing sets over broad rules
steps.sub: scoped to the visitor's own session context

code:
Pattern behind real exposures:
  broad access granted during testing
  -> never narrowed before launch
  -> reachable by anyone, no login needed

The fix: the same discipline, just
applied BEFORE launch.
caption: Never a clever fix — the same start-restrictive principle from Lesson 19.

subtitle: Protecting the sessions authenticated users actually have.
